subject: Re: Pen test follow-up — evidence & containment for credential/session exposure
messages:
From: HorizonBank Security <security@horizonbank.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@horizonbank.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jan 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pen test report and confirmation of fixes — HorizonBank account

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking our penetration test report. We have a couple of high-priority asks so we can close the open items on our side and update our risk register:

- Can you confirm the final report (we received an excerpt but not the full findings list) and the exact scope of systems that were tested? We need that for our audit.
- For Finding 3 (credential/token exposure in logs / session token leakage), please provide:
  * A brief summary of the root cause you identified
  * Containment steps already taken (rotations, session invalidation, log redaction) with timestamps
  * Planned code-level remediation ETA and owners
  * Artifacts: keystore rotation logs, ticket IDs for any code fix, and any firewall/WAF rules applied

If you can provide the above by EOD Mon (PST) it will help us keep the remediation deadline for our compliance window.

We appreciate quick confirmation that tokens are no longer being emitted in plain text to logs and any temporary mitigations in place.

Regards,
HorizonBank Security
security@horizonbank.com

Attachment: pen_test_excerpt.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference.com>
To: HorizonBank Security <security@horizonbank.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pen test report and confirmation of fixes — HorizonBank account

Hi — thanks for the clear list. Quick acknowledgement and plan below.

Summary/root cause (short): the pen test flagged a legacy debug path that emitted truncated bearer strings into structured logs when debug-level tracing was enabled for specific deployments. This occurred only for a small subset of requests routed through an older gateway shim that lacked the new log-sanitizer.

Containment already completed (timestamps):
- 2027-01-30T09:05Z: rotated affected API consumer keys and decreased token TTLs for the impacted customer scope (rotation log attached).
- 2027-01-30T09:20Z: invalidated active sessions issued under the affected tokens and forced re-auth for active connectors.
- 2027-01-30T09:40Z: pushed a WAF rule to block requests matching the shim's fingerprint (temporary mitigation).
- 2027-01-30T10:00Z: disabled debug-level tracing for the affected deployment group.

Planned remediation (owners & ETA):
- Engineering ticket SEC-1427 created (owner: Priyom Das, SRE/Platform) — scope: remove legacy shim, add runtime log-sanitizer enforcement, add CI check to prevent debug leak regressions.
- Target for code-level fix and deploy to prod: 2027-02-12 (two-week ETA).
- Post-deploy verification and evidence handoff: 2027-02-14.

Artifacts attached: authn_fix_checklist.csv (checklist of containment steps), pt_report_excerpt.pdf (our copy of the findings), keystore-rotation-log-20270131.txt (rotation audit). We'll also upload diffs and CI logs to the secure evidence Drive link.

I'll loop Priyom below for the technical artifact set; Irene will coordinate the SOC2 evidence package if you need the control mapping.

Next steps:
- Priyom: will send the keystore rotation extract and a signed verification of session invalidation.
- Irene: will prepare SOC2 control mapping for this finding and flag any changes to the evidence matrix.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Security Programs Manager — Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0129

Attachment: authn_fix_checklist.csv (text/csv)
